original_query: SELECT t6.NAME FROM (SELECT JOB FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY JOB) AS t5 LEFT JOIN (SELECT NAME FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME) AS t6 ON t5.JOB = t6.NAME GROUP BY t6.NAME
rewritten_query:
SELECT DISTINCT d.NAME
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT JOB
    FROM EMP
    WHERE ENAME = 'A'
) e
LEFT JOIN DEPT d
    ON e.JOB = d.NAME;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Removed the pre-aggregated derived table on DEPT (SELECT NAME FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME). The final SELECT DISTINCT already collapses duplicate DEPT names, allowing the optimizer to use a direct join (e.g., index lookup on DEPT.NAME) instead of aggregating all 450,000 dept rows before the join.

Replaced the outer GROUP BY t6.NAME with SELECT DISTINCT. The outer GROUP BY was redundant for matched rows (both inputs were already unique per JOB/NAME) and only served to collapse multiple NULL rows; SELECT DISTINCT preserves this semantics with less overhead.
Kept the selective filter ENAME = 'A' pushed directly into the EMP derived table so it is applied early, before deduplication and joining.

Changed the join from two pre-aggregated subqueries to: (1) deduplicate EMP jobs for ENAME='A' early, then (2) LEFT JOIN directly to DEPT. This lets the planner use an index nested-loop join on DEPT(NAME) when EMP rows are few.
